target_customer: Enterprises needing visibility and control over AI agents and MCP servers
problem: Companies cannot see which AI agents and MCP tools are connected, or enforce policy and audit trails over them.
business_model: Open source framework (GolfMCP) with a paid hosted gateway and enterprise governance
product_category: AI agent and MCP security and governance

founders.name: Wojciech Błaszak
previous_startups: First company started at 14, reached $200k revenue per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Gateway, tracing and policy enforcement for a new protocol are standard infrastructure work with fast moving specs.

defensibility.rationale: Open source framework and a crowded set of gateway vendors make copying easy; enterprise trust and certifications may add some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Other MCP gateways raised seeds in 2025 (Runlayer $11M, Obot $35M); no source shows Golf copied or bought.

market_need_then: The founders say they spoke with over 40 teams building MCP servers before launching, and MCP adoption by enterprises grew in 2025.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand was found; GolfMCP exists as an open source project name.

outcome_analysis: Golf is an active Spring 2025 company that moved from an open source MCP framework to an enterprise control plane in early 2026. Funding and traction are not independently verified, and well funded MCP security rivals appeared in the same year, so the story is still open.
notes: A $500K figure from EveryDev is unverified (single aggregator) and not recorded as a round. SOC 2 claim comes from a single profile. No dated competitor source near April 2025 was found, so the list is empty. Completeness pass: Round rests on a single database (Startupintros) and a matching EveryDev figure; company identity on Startupintros is not fully confirmed.
